findings.claim: MessagePack attributes on the formatted type are ignored in the normal, non-surrogate path. The collector unconditionally calls CreateContractlessMembers and forces string keys, without inspecting T for MessagePackObject, Key, or IgnoreMember. Consequently, a referenced type with [Key(0)] and [IgnoreMember] is serialized as a contractless map including the ignored member, contrary to the acceptance criterion that MessagePack attributes on T be honoured.

receipt_plan.detail: Run GeneratedMessagePackFormatterRequirementTests.MessagePackAttributesOnReferencedType_AreHonoured. It generates a formatter for a referenced [MessagePackObject] type with one [Key(0)] member and one [IgnoreMember] member, then asserts an array formatter with key 0 and no serialization of the ignored member. The current contractless map implementation fails these assertions.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Use the implemented surrogate design: GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute exposes SurrogateType, the generator defaults to contractless public-member serialization, and when a surrogate is supplied its [Key] and [IgnoreMember] members select and key matching members of T. This requires the SurrogateType public API, surrogate collector path, and MsgPack022 diagnostics.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Use BCL serialization attributes on T instead of introducing a surrogate contract: remove SurrogateType and its collector path, serialize unattributed types contractlessly, honour MessagePack attributes when present, and when T is [DataContract], derive membership and ordering from [DataMember] and [IgnoreDataMember]. This keeps Project A dependent only on the BCL while providing an explicit external wire contract.
